detail.title: Operational Criteria for Physical Causal Memory
detail.summary: Causal memory is defined as a persistent physical state that compresses historical observations to improve future predictive performance. This notebook synthesizes findings showing that coarse-graining, while necessary for operational tractability, imposes fundamental lower bounds on entropy production. Environmental redundancy serves as a mechanism to balance system noise with retrieval fidelity, while feedback-aided surfaces demonstrate that dynamic control can reduce thermodynamic dissipation in predictive engines.
detail.reason: Notebook updated to incorporate evidence on coarse-graining and effective redundancy.
